en: Abstract
zh: 摘要

en: This article places maritime violence at the center of the history of international ordering. It views the transformation of the nineteenth-century Atlantic from the deck of one ship, a Baltimore-built privateer called the

The ship’s captain seized Spanish and Portuguese shipping under a privateering commission from the Oriental Republic. Sponsorship of privateers by the Oriental Republic and other new Latin American governments reflected an open-ended Atlantic constitutionalism that recognized sovereignty at multiple scales. That constitutional context formed the background to three cases involving the

and its crew that reached the U.S. Supreme Court. The cases show how privateering politics opened to wide-ranging debates about the definition of states, war, and piracy, while preserving the indeterminacies of sovereignty in the new Atlantic system. That system, closing as it formed, was composed of new states pressured to align with powerful empires. Privateering disputes featured sharpening rhetoric about piracy as a crime under the law of nations while at the same time preserving a regime that protected low-level maritime violence. Situating the politics of piracy at the nexus of domestic and international orders, the article highlights the political uses and legal limits of the discourse of pirates as enemies of all and connects this history to an understanding of terrorism and states in the international order.
zh: 本文把海上暴力置于国际秩序形成史的中心，从一艘船的甲板上观察十九世纪大西洋的转变：这是一艘在巴尔的摩建造、名为

的私掠船。该船船长持东方共和国颁发的私掠委任状，捕获西班牙和葡萄牙船只。东方共和国及其他拉丁美洲新政府对私掠船的支持，体现了一种承认多种尺度上主权的开放式大西洋宪政主义。这一宪政背景，构成涉及“不可抗拒号”及其船员、最终提交美国最高法院的三起案件的背景。这些案件表明，私掠政治如何引出关于国家、战争和海盗行为定义的广泛辩论，同时保留了新大西洋体系中主权的不确定性。这一体系在形成的同时趋于封闭，由受到压力、必须与强大帝国协调立场的新国家构成。围绕私掠的争议，一方面强化了把海盗行为视为万国法之下犯罪的修辞，另一方面又保留了保护低烈度海上暴力的制度。本文把海盗政治置于国内秩序与国际秩序的交汇处，突出“海盗是所有人的敌人”这一话语的政治用途和法律限度，并把这段历史同理解国际秩序中的恐怖主义与国家联系起来。

en: For much of the last two decades, historians of piracy have been caught in a cycle of myth-making and myth-busting.

One group of scholars, joined by popular writers eager to profit from the robust market for pirate lore, depicts maritime raiders as colorful rogues. They portray most pirates as inherently anti-authoritarian actors who possessed a penchant for experimenting with alternative forms of political solidarity. Histories in this vein highlight early modern pirates’ pacts to share booty and their rituals for overturning rule by despotic captains. Some accounts credit pirates with founding radically innovative republics or depict them as footloose maritime raiders who contributed to Enlightenment thought, aided democratic revolutions, and fueled anti-imperial movements. Campaigns against piracy become, in this telling, synonymous with other forms of state oppression.
zh: 在过去二十年的大部分时间里，海盗史学家一直陷于制造神话与打破神话的循环。

一批学者，以及急于从旺盛的海盗传说市场中获利的通俗作家，把海上劫掠者描绘成富有传奇色彩的无赖。他们把大多数海盗描述为本质上反权威的行动者，偏好尝试另类的政治团结形式。这类历史强调近代早期海盗分享战利品的盟约，以及推翻专横船长统治的仪式。有些叙述把建立激进创新共和国的功劳归于海盗，或者把他们描绘为无牵无挂的海上劫掠者，认为他们促成了启蒙思想、协助了民主革命，并推动了反帝国运动。在这套叙述中，打击海盗的行动，便成为其他形式国家压迫的同义词。

en: A second group of historians has critiqued representations of pirates as political innovators, revealing their connections to established, if fluid, networks of patronage and power. These scholars show that most early modern raiders claimed to be not pirates but privateers—mariners licensed by legitimate sovereigns to seize enemy ships. Studies track how raiders engaged actively in what I have called “legal posturing” to color their actions as lawful and improve their chances of securing booty as property. Rather than fomenting revolution, most raiders cultivated powerful sponsors and aspired to positions as propertied heads of household in settled communities. Campaigns against piracy had various political objectives and creatively deployed rhetoric about pirates as enemies of all, but polities mainly sought to contain piracy through its criminalization under domestic law.
zh: 另一批历史学家批评了把海盗描绘为政治创新者的做法，揭示他们与既有的、尽管不断变化的庇护和权力网络之间的联系。这些学者表明，大多数近代早期劫掠者声称自己并非海盗，而是私掠者——获合法主权者许可、可以捕获敌方船只的海员。相关研究追踪了劫掠者如何积极采取我所称的“法律姿态”，为自己的行动涂上合法色彩，提高把战利品确认为财产的机会。大多数劫掠者并不煽动革命，而是结交强大的资助者，渴望在定居社群中成为有产户主。打击海盗的行动具有多种政治目标，也创造性地运用了“海盗是所有人的敌人”的修辞；但各政治体主要还是通过国内法将海盗行为刑事化，以遏制海盗活动。

en: Having participated in developing the second perspective, I have had reason to despair over the resilience of the first. No assemblage of evidence seems capable of dislodging the view that pirates were anti-authoritarian rogues routinely regarded as enemies of all. Nor does it appear to matter that the doctrinal force of the language of universal enmity changed over time.

The finding that campaigns to contain raiding relied more on actions under domestic law than on the exercise of universal jurisdiction has also not slowed the production of romanticized pirate histories.

Paradoxically, chiseling away at the image of the outcast pirate has perhaps helped focus attention on the figure of the sea raider rather than encouraging analysis of the institutional context that structured maritime relations.
zh: 作为第二种视角的参与建构者，我有理由对第一种视角的顽强生命力感到绝望。似乎无论汇集多少证据，都无法撼动这样的看法：海盗是反权威的无赖，通常被视为所有人的敌人。“普遍敌对”语言在法律学说上的效力曾随时间变化，这一点似乎也无关紧要。
研究发现，遏制海上劫掠的行动更多依靠国内法下的措施，而非普遍管辖权的行使；这一发现，也未能减缓浪漫化海盗史的生产。
悖谬的是，不断削弱“被放逐的海盗”这一形象，或许反而使注意力集中在海上劫掠者这个人物身上，而未能鼓励人们分析组织海上关系的制度背景。

en: Several lines of inquiry disrupt these debates by underscoring the political significance of maritime raiding. One strand explores the relation of maritime violence to state formation. Historians have tracked the effects of piracy on political authority in such diverse contexts as the ancient Mediterranean, sixteenth-century South Asia, and the early nineteenth-century United States.
A closely related strand of research investigates the place of piracy in the rise of regional and global orders.
Lisa Ford and I have traced, for example, how imperial and interimperial maritime campaigns to contain piracy helped produce gap-ridden, jurisdictionally complex legal regimes of oceanic dimensions.
zh: 若干研究路径强调海上劫掠的政治意义，从而打破了上述辩论的格局。其中一条路径探究海上暴力与国家形成的关系。历史学家追踪了海盗行为在古代地中海、十六世纪南亚以及十九世纪早期美国等不同情境中，对政治权威产生的影响。
与之密切相关的另一条路径，考察海盗行为在区域与全球秩序兴起中的位置。
例如，莉萨·福特和我曾追踪帝国及帝国之间为遏制海盗而开展的海上行动，如何促成覆盖大洋、漏洞重重且管辖关系复杂的法律制度。

en: This article builds on legal-political approaches to piracy to examine maritime raiding and the rise of the international Atlantic. Setting aside older debates about pirates centered on piracy’s so-called golden age, I analyze the connections between a surge in Atlantic raiding and the proliferation of states in the early nineteenth century. The inquiry requires some critical distance from narratives about the Age of Revolutions as a period in which a “wave” of revolutionary ideology or a “contagion of sovereignty” transformed the region.

As Christopher Clark notes in relation to the global political upheavals of 1848, revolutions did not always respond to global currents but instead developed as “cognate” events that unfolded “within kindred cultural and political orders.”

In the early nineteenth-century Atlantic, new political entities formed in sync in response to imperial tensions and war, in particular the crisis created by the French invasion of the Iberian Peninsula. An open-ended constitutionalism framed a variety of possible political formations, and new entities grappled with imperial governments that sought in some ways to foster and in other ways to obstruct or limit the formation of new sovereignties.
zh: 本文以研究海盗行为的法律—政治路径为基础，考察海上劫掠与国际性大西洋的兴起。我暂且搁置围绕所谓海盗黄金时代展开的旧有辩论，分析十九世纪早期大西洋劫掠激增与国家数量增加之间的联系。这一探究需要与某些关于革命时代的叙述保持批判距离：这些叙述将该时期描绘为革命意识形态的“浪潮”或“主权的传染”改变了整个地区的时代。
正如克里斯托弗·克拉克就1848年全球政治动荡指出的，革命并不总是在回应全球潮流，而可能作为“同源的”事件，在“相近的文化与政治秩序之内”展开。
在十九世纪早期的大西洋地区，新的政治实体同步形成，回应着帝国紧张关系与战争，尤其是法国入侵伊比利亚半岛所造成的危机。开放式宪政主义为多种可能的政治组织形式提供了框架；新实体则与帝国政府周旋，后者一方面试图推动、另一方面又试图阻挠或限制新主权的形成。

en: There was also more to the region’s political transformation than a set of cognate events. A perceived urgency to establish claims to international belonging gripped the region. Diplomats, merchants, officials, mariners, laborers, and captives surveyed international events and pressures with intense interest and positioned themselves in relation to these changes. Explaining political reordering on an oceanic scale in the period requires close attention to the interpenetration of domestic and international political arenas.
It depends, that is, on treating the international order as something other than an already constituted realm hovering beyond the horizon of local, national, and regional politics.
zh: 这一地区的政治转变，也不止是一组同源事件。确立自身属于国际社会之主张的紧迫感，笼罩着整个地区。外交官、商人、官员、海员、劳动者与俘虏，都高度关注国际事件及其压力，并依据这些变化为自己定位。要解释这一时期大洋尺度上的政治重组，就必须密切关注国内与国际政治场域的相互渗透。
也就是说，不能把国际秩序当作一个已经构成的领域，仿佛它悬浮于地方、国家和区域政治的视野之外。

en: This perspective shifts attention away from questions about whether pirates were insiders or outsiders. In this period as in others, the key characteristic of maritime raiding was its flickering quality, the fundamental instability of its legal protections.
Like constitutionalism itself, legal practices of privateering and piracy opened simultaneously toward domestic (national or imperial) and international ordering.

Just as disputes inside polities altered the conditions under which booty could be turned into property, imperial politics informed judgments about which states might be recognized as legitimate sponsors of raiding. Multi-sited conflicts about sea raiding transformed an Atlantic of proliferating political experiments into a regional system of unequal states under imperial sway.
zh: 这一视角把注意力从海盗究竟是内部人还是外部人的问题上移开。在这一时期，正如其他时期一样，海上劫掠的关键特征，是其忽明忽暗的性质，即其法律保护根本上的不稳定。
正如宪政主义本身，私掠与海盗行为的法律实践，同时朝向国内（国家或帝国）秩序和国际秩序的形成。
政治体内部的争议改变了战利品转化为财产的条件；同样，帝国政治也影响着哪些国家可被承认为劫掠行动合法支持者的判断。围绕海上劫掠在多个地点发生的冲突，把一个政治试验不断增多的大西洋，转变成处于帝国影响之下、由不平等国家构成的区域体系。

en: Privateering disputes were at the heart of this process. To trace their effects, this article views the changes in the Atlantic order from the deck of one ship. It follows the
and its enterprising Baltimore captain, John Daniels, on a pair of cruises to capture Iberian vessels between 1818 and 1822.

Daniels sailed with a privateering commission from the Oriental Republic, a confederation led by the Banda Oriental, also known as the Provincia Oriental, a former territory of the Spanish empire in the Río de la Plata region. After Daniels returned to Baltimore with his booty, Portuguese and Spanish consuls challenged the captures, and Daniels also faced criminal prosecution. Scores of crew members of the
who had joined a mutiny and led raids were tried and convicted of piracy. Three cases stemming from the captures of the

—two prize cases and one criminal case—reached the U.S. Supreme Court and stimulated debates about much larger issues than the question of whether Daniels could keep his booty: What was a state? What was the difference between war and rebellion? What was the legal definition of piracy?
zh: 私掠争议处于这一过程的核心。为追踪其影响，本文从一艘船的甲板观察大西洋秩序的变化。文章跟随
及其富于进取心的巴尔的摩船长约翰·丹尼尔斯，考察他在1818至1822年间两次捕获伊比利亚船只的巡航。

丹尼尔斯持有东方共和国颁发的私掠委任状。东方共和国是一个由东岸地区（Banda Oriental，亦称东方省Provincia Oriental）领导的邦联；东岸原为西班牙帝国在拉普拉塔河地区的领土。丹尼尔斯携战利品返回巴尔的摩后，葡萄牙和西班牙领事对这些捕获提出异议，丹尼尔斯还面临刑事起诉。“不可抗拒号”上数十名参与哗变并带头劫掠的船员，被以海盗罪审判并定罪。由“不可抗拒号”的捕获行为引出的三起案件——两起捕获物案件和一起刑事案件——提交至美国最高法院，并引发了远超丹尼尔斯能否保留战利品这一问题的辩论：什么是国家？战争与叛乱有何区别？海盗行为的法律定义是什么？

en: These questions emerged at a pivotal time in the formation of the international Atlantic. Following the

, we spy an international order closing as it formed. When Daniels began his cruise, the region was crowded with political experiments, including juntas, city-states, confederations, and self-proclaimed nations. When the U.S. Supreme Court issued rulings about the
and its captures, only a handful of new polities had acquired the status of nation-states. International recognition had become an offer that political communities and their leaders could not refuse.

Yet even as they received a measure of recognition, new states struggled to define and expand their sovereign capacities, and imperial governments retained enormous influence over this process. The new Atlantic system was a system of sovereign states with formal equality but vast differences in the capacity and right to make war.
zh: 这些问题出现于国际性大西洋形成的关键时刻。循着
的航迹，我们看到一个在形成同时趋于封闭的国际秩序。丹尼尔斯开始巡航时，这一地区充满各种政治试验，包括政务委员会、城邦、邦联和自称的民族国家。当美国最高法院就“不可抗拒号”及其捕获物作出判决时，只有少数新政治体取得了民族国家地位。国际承认已成为政治共同体及其领导人无法拒绝的提议。
然而，即便获得了一定程度的承认，新国家仍在艰难地界定和扩展其主权能力，而帝国政府对这一过程依然拥有巨大影响。新的大西洋体系，是一个主权国家体系；各国形式上平等，但发动战争的能力与权利却相差悬殊。

en: The emerging Atlantic order comprised a regime of limited violence that preserved a space for sea raiding. Empires leaned on American states to contain privateering, but few advocated banning it completely. The policy of slow, partial recognition of insurgent governments meant that the British government had to refrain from classing all South American raiders as pirates. The Spanish government, meanwhile, exerted strong pressure on U.S. officials to curb privateering while also sponsoring corsair raids of its own, particularly in the waters around Cuba. The result of these trends was that rhetoric about piracy as a crime under the law of nations was becoming sharper at the same time that protections of low-level maritime violence were being carefully preserved and revised. Becoming international in the Atlantic meant achieving membership in a stratified interpolity order under interimperial regulation and subject to the continued threat of imperial violence.
zh: 正在形成的大西洋秩序包含一套有限暴力制度，为海上劫掠保留了空间。帝国向美洲各国施压，要求遏制私掠，但很少有人主张完全禁止私掠。缓慢、部分承认起义政府的政策，意味着英国政府必须避免把所有南美洲劫掠者都归为海盗。与此同时，西班牙政府一面强力施压美国官员，要求限制私掠，一面又支持自身的私掠袭击，尤其是在古巴周边海域。这些趋势的结果，是在把海盗行为视为万国法之下犯罪的修辞日益尖锐的同时，对低烈度海上暴力的保护仍被谨慎保留并不断调整。在大西洋地区成为国际社会的一员，意味着进入一个分层的政治体间秩序：这一秩序受到帝国间的规制，并始终面对帝国暴力的威胁。

en: Atlantic sea raiding and its regulation also brought some unintended consequences. Slave traders obtained and used privateering licenses, and counterrevolutionaries borrowed arguments about insurgent states’ right to make war. Like the capacious use of “terrorism,” the label of piracy was deployed mainly to degrade the status of sponsors of sea raiding within the international order rather than to position groups outside it. Despite claims about its foundational legal significance, ringing rhetoric about pirates as enemies of all derived its meaning from the politics of international ordering.
zh: 大西洋海上劫掠及其规制，也带来了一些意外后果。奴隶贩子获得并使用私掠许可证，反革命者则借用了起义国家有权发动战争的论证。与“恐怖主义”一词的宽泛用法类似，“海盗”标签的主要用途，是降低海上劫掠支持者在国际秩序中的地位，而不是把某些群体置于秩序之外。尽管有人宣称“海盗是所有人的敌人”具有基础性的法律意义，这种响亮修辞的含义，仍来自国际秩序形成的政治。

en: Atlantic Constitutionalism
zh: 大西洋宪政主义

en: Our story begins not in Baltimore, the home port of John Daniels, but on the banks of the Río de la Plata, where a fluid constitutionalism framed responses to the collapse of the Spanish monarchy after the French invasion of the Iberian Peninsula. When a junta formed in Buenos Aires in 1810 to fill the political void, the scope of its authority across former Spanish territories remained uncertain. A set of provincial leaders and their followers were reluctant to trade rule by European empires for the dominance of port elites, and all groups were responding to the persisting threat of imperial attack and annexation.
zh: 我们的故事并非始于约翰·丹尼尔斯的母港巴尔的摩，而是始于拉普拉塔河畔。在那里，法国入侵伊比利亚半岛后，西班牙君主制崩溃；流动不定的宪政主义为回应这一崩溃提供了框架。1810年，布宜诺斯艾利斯成立政务委员会，以填补政治真空，但它在原西班牙各领土上的权力范围仍不确定。一些省级领袖及其追随者，不愿用港口精英的支配来替代欧洲帝国的统治；所有群体也都在回应帝国进攻和吞并的持续威胁。

en: One result was political fragmentation. On land bordering the Río Uruguay and the Río de la Plata, a war-tested colonel named José Gervasio Artigas joined the fight against loyalist Spanish forces concentrated at Montevideo, then engineered a break with Buenos Aires. Even before the 1815 rupture, Artigas was laying the groundwork for the territory’s semi-autonomy. At the beginning of 1813, when the second triumvirate to rule Buenos Aires called a Constituent Assembly, Artigas issued a set of instructions to delegates from the Banda Oriental. The instructions provide a primer of Artiguista thought—a constitutionalism that left open the possibility of sovereignty at multiple scales.
zh: 其结果之一，是政治分裂。在乌拉圭河与拉普拉塔河沿岸，一位久经战阵的上校何塞·赫尔瓦西奥·阿蒂加斯，加入了对抗集中于蒙得维的亚的西班牙保王派军队的战斗，随后又策划与布宜诺斯艾利斯决裂。早在1815年正式决裂之前，阿蒂加斯便已为该地区的半自治奠定基础。1813年初，统治布宜诺斯艾利斯的第二届三人执政团召开制宪会议时，阿蒂加斯向东岸地区的代表发出一套训令。这些训令提供了阿蒂加斯主义思想的入门纲要：一种为多个尺度上的主权保留可能性的宪政主义。

en: Artigas assigned the government of the United Provinces a limited set of capacities and proposed reserving some sovereign authority for the Banda Oriental. The United Provinces would assume key prerogatives, including the right to establish “fundamental laws” regulating relations among provinces; the right to represent the provinces in most—but not all—dealings with foreign powers; and the right to organize collective defense and maintain provincial military forces. Artigas supported these claims by stating that sovereignty resided in the people (
) and was delegated, in different measure, to his government and to the government of the United Provinces.
zh: 阿蒂加斯赋予联合省政府一组有限的职能，并提议为东岸地区保留部分主权权力。联合省将承担关键特权，包括制定规范省际关系的“根本法”的权利；在与外国势力的大多数——但并非全部——交往中代表各省的权利；以及组织共同防御、维持各省武装力量的权利。阿蒂加斯以如下说法支持这些主张：主权属于人民（
），并以不同程度委托给他的政府和联合省政府。

en: Artigas’s instructions to the delegates from the Provincia Oriental drew from eclectic sources. The twenty articles include text paraphrasing passages from the U.S. Declaration of Independence, the Articles of Confederation, the Constitutions of Virginia and Massachusetts, and the U.S. Constitution.

The document resembled a declaration of independence in that it announced the dissolution of ties between the colonies and the Spanish monarchy and established the existence of the Provincia Oriental as a sovereign entity.

Paraphrasing the U.S. Articles of Confederation and the Constitution of Massachusetts, Article 11 stated that the Provincia Oriental would “retain its sovereignty, liberty, and independence, all power, jurisdiction, and rights not delegated explicitly by the Confederation of the United Provinces at the Congress.”
Article 10 characterized the pact among provinces as “a firm bond of friendship.”
zh: 阿蒂加斯向东方省代表发出的训令，博采多种来源。二十条训令中的文本，改写了美国《独立宣言》《邦联条例》、弗吉尼亚州与马萨诸塞州宪法，以及美国宪法中的段落。
这份文件类似于独立宣言，因为它宣布解除殖民地与西班牙君主制之间的纽带，并确立东方省作为主权实体的存在。
第11条改写美国《邦联条例》和马萨诸塞州宪法，指出东方省将“保留其主权、自由与独立，以及联合省邦联在大会上未明确委托的一切权力、管辖权和权利”。
第10条把各省之间的契约称为“牢固的友谊纽带”。

en: Around the time that he issued the instructions, Artigas explained that a variety of constitutional designs would be consistent with the recognition that sovereignty resided in the people. Addressing his followers, Artigas proclaimed that his own authority “emanates from you and ceases with your sovereign presence.”

The authority of the Constituent Assembly, he stated, did not flow from the transfer of the people’s loyalty from the Spanish crown to the new government. The assembly’s legitimacy could derive only from a pact that left the liberty of the provinces intact, and the foundation of any new political regime would also depend on the authority of
. Artigas styled himself the
and explained to one delegate, “The particular sovereignty of the
will be explicitly declared and sustained as the singular object of our revolution.”

Although in theory the sovereignty of free peoples might be assigned to authorities at any level, Artigas regarded towns as political entities with special legitimacy. The phrase “pueblos libres” referred unambiguously to the sovereignty of the people (
), but it also evoked the view that the smallest settlements (towns or
) were repositories of sovereignty close to the people—an idea that represented, as one scholar noted decades ago, “the essence of Artiguista thought.”
zh: 在发布训令的前后，阿蒂加斯解释说，多种宪制设计都可以与主权在民的承认相一致。面对追随者，他宣称自己的权威“源自你们，并在作为主权者的你们亲临时终止”。
他指出，制宪会议的权威，并非来自人民将对西班牙王室的忠诚转移给新政府。会议的合法性只能来自一个保全各省自由的契约；任何新政治体制的基础，也都依赖
的权威。阿蒂加斯自称
（自由人民／自由城镇的保护者），并向一位代表解释：“
的各自主权，将被明确宣告并维护，作为我们革命的唯一目标。”
尽管在理论上，自由人民的主权可以委托给任何层级的权力机关，阿蒂加斯仍认为，城镇是具有特殊合法性的政治实体。“pueblos libres”这一短语，毫不含糊地指向人民（
）的主权，同时又唤起这样一种看法：最小的聚落，即城镇或
，是接近人民的主权存放之所。正如一位学者数十年前所指出的，这一观念代表了“阿蒂加斯主义思想的精髓”。

en: Artigas was not founding a nation.
Nor did he intend, with his extensive use of U.S. constitutional documents, merely to adapt a U.S. model of statehood.

That model was, in any case, full of ambiguities and not easy to appropriate. The United States was a hotbed of constitutional conflicts, not yet organized around the dyad of federal and state governments but involving a jumble of claimants to authority, including “towns, cities, and assemblies of private citizens.”
The country was also entering a slow-burning constitutional crisis centered on the extension of slavery to western territories.

Artigas was drawn to U.S. texts precisely because they affirmed the possibility of multiple configurations of sovereignty, flexibility that was was necessary to his political survival in the face of imperial aggression.
zh: 阿蒂加斯并不是在建立一个民族国家。
他大量援引美国宪制文件，也并非仅仅为了改造和采用美国的国家模式。
无论如何，这一模式本身充满歧义，并不容易借用。美国是宪制冲突的温床，尚未围绕联邦政府与州政府这一二元结构组织起来，而是牵涉一大批权威主张者，包括“城镇、城市和私人公民的集会”。
该国也正进入一场缓慢发酵的宪制危机，核心是奴隶制向西部领土的扩展。
阿蒂加斯之所以受到美国文本吸引，恰恰因为它们肯定主权可以具有多种配置；面对帝国侵略，这种灵活性是他在政治上生存所必需的。

en: Multiple threats were looming. Artiguistas faced the likelihood of invasion by Luso-Brazilian forces, the danger of re-conquest by a resurgent Spanish empire, and the possibility that the British, who had invaded in 1806–1807, might take advantage of regional strife to mount another attempt at occupation. These conditions heightened interest in achieving international recognition.
In service to that goal and to fortify the polity’s ability to defend itself, Artigas claimed the right to make war, including the authority to sponsor privateering.
zh: 多重威胁正在逼近。阿蒂加斯派面临葡萄牙—巴西军队入侵的可能、复兴中的西班牙帝国重新征服的危险，以及英国利用地区纷争再次谋求占领的可能——英国曾在1806至1807年入侵。这些条件增强了取得国际承认的意愿。
为实现这一目标，并强化该政治体的自卫能力，阿蒂加斯主张发动战争的权利，其中包括支持私掠的权力。

en: Privateering in Atlantic Politics
zh: 大西洋政治中的私掠

en: Artigas looked out on an ocean of raiding. By the second half of the eighteenth century, conventions for adjudicating captures of ships in wartime were relatively consistent across the Atlantic world. Each empire had its own prize courts, and captors were supposed to sail captured ships and their cargoes to their own courts for adjudication. In theory, all claimants, regardless of nationality, could present evidence that ships or cargoes had been seized unlawfully and should be returned.
zh: 阿蒂加斯面对的是一片劫掠之海。到十八世纪下半叶，大西洋世界各地关于战时船只捕获的裁判惯例，已相对一致。每个帝国都有自己的捕获法庭，捕获者应将被俘船只及其货物驶送至己方的法庭裁判。理论上，所有权利主张者，不分国籍，都可以提出证据，证明船只或货物系被非法扣押，应予归还。

en: This relatively stable interpolity framework coexisted with a jumble of evasive practices. Ship owners, merchants, and mariners maneuvered to sidestep legal requirements or conform to them only on paper. Sea raiders creatively interpreted the terms of their commissions, and they sometimes did not take their captures to prize courts, or they presented their booty in courts of uncertain jurisdiction where captures could be adjudicated quickly and without close scrutiny of evidence. Captains and their sponsors were equally adept at legal maneuvering. It was possible to purchase privateering commissions and to alter the nationality of ships and goods by changing owners on paper or by transferring goods to neutral vessels before entering ports. A surge in enemy ships sailing as neutrals confounded the system, with international coalitions favoring different legal approaches to neutral shipping in wartime.
Incentives to profit from prizes stimulated the proliferation of prize courts around the region, with some remaining active in periods of relative interimperial peace.
zh: 这一相对稳定的政治体间框架，与种种规避行为并存。船东、商人与海员设法绕开法律要求，或仅在纸面上遵守。海上劫掠者创造性地解释委任状的条款，有时不把捕获物送交捕获法庭，或将战利品送至管辖权存疑的法庭，在那里，捕获可以迅速获得裁决，证据也不会受到仔细审查。船长及其支持者同样擅长法律操作。私掠委任状可以买到；船只与货物的国籍，也可通过在纸面上变更所有者，或在进港前把货物转移到中立船只上而改变。伪装为中立船航行的敌方船只激增，使这一制度陷入混乱，而不同国际联盟对战时中立航运的法律处理持不同立场。
从捕获物中获利的动机，刺激了这一地区捕获法庭数量的增长，其中一些在帝国间相对和平的时期仍持续运作。

en: Recognizing opportunities in this fluid system, new Latin American governments quickly began to license privateers and dispatch recruiters to North American ports. In 1816, American citizen Thomas Taylor arrived in Baltimore as an envoy of the Buenos Aires government carrying a small number of blank commissions, which he either gave or—much more likely—sold to Baltimore mariners. Other South American agents followed, and news surged through South and North American ports about opportunities to raid for new governments against Spanish shipping.
zh: 拉丁美洲的新政府认识到这一流动制度中的机会，迅速开始向私掠者发放许可，并派招募人员前往北美港口。1816年，美国公民托马斯·泰勒作为布宜诺斯艾利斯政府使节抵达巴尔的摩，携带少量空白委任状；他把这些委任状交给——更可能是卖给——巴尔的摩的海员。其他南美洲代理人随后而来；为新政府劫掠西班牙船只的机会，迅速成为南北美洲港口中流传的消息。

en: In the Río de la Plata, privateers were vital to defense. In 1815, after his forces had expelled Buenos Aires troops from Montevideo, Artigas led the movement to form the Liga Federal (Federal League), a confederation of the Banda Oriental and the provinces of Córdoba, Corrientes, Entre Ríos, Misiones, and Santa Fe. In 1816, he began to issue

(privateering commissions) listing Artigas as “the Chief of the Orientales and Protector of the Peoples of the República Oriental” and instructing holders to “respect the Flag of the Republic and attack its enemies in the manner judged most opportune according to the Law of Nations.”

The use of the “República Oriental” on the privateering commissions was intentional and strategic. It identified the confederation as an international entity with the right to make war and announced Artigas as a head of state. The practice was consistent with Artigas’s use of “República Oriental” only in external communications and of “Banda Oriental” and “Provincia Oriental” on documents circulating within the territory and region.

The bifurcation could also work against him. Luso-Brazilian officials would insist on representing Artigas as the head of the Banda Oriental, not the confederation, and the more limited designation was adopted by U.S. courts and U.S. government officials.
zh: 在拉普拉塔河地区，私掠者对防务至关重要。1815年，阿蒂加斯的部队将布宜诺斯艾利斯军队逐出蒙得维的亚后，他领导组建Liga Federal（联邦同盟），即由东岸地区与科尔多瓦、科连特斯、恩特雷里奥斯、米西奥内斯和圣菲诸省组成的邦联。1816年，他开始颁发
（私掠委任状），把自己列为“东方人的首领与东方共和国人民的保护者”，并指示持有人“尊重共和国旗帜，依照万国法，以被认为最适当的方式攻击其敌人”。
私掠委任状使用“República Oriental”（东方共和国）这一名称，是有意而且具有策略性的。它把邦联标示为具有战争权的国际实体，并宣布阿蒂加斯为国家元首。这一做法，与阿蒂加斯仅在对外交往中使用“República Oriental”、而在领土内部及地区内流通的文件中使用“Banda Oriental”和“Provincia Oriental”的习惯一致。
这种两分也可能对他不利。葡萄牙—巴西官员坚持把阿蒂加斯描述为东岸地区的首脑，而非邦联首脑；美国法院和政府官员也采纳了这一更有限的称谓。

en: Captains quickly learned about the peculiar value of the commissions signed by Artigas. Whereas commissions from the government of the United Provinces specified that privateers could attack only Spanish ships, Artigas’s

authorized captures of both Portuguese and Spanish vessels, opening to privateers the possibility of tapping into the lucrative trade from Brazil and Asia to Portugal. But there were downsides and dangers. The commissions were not accepted in Buenos Aires prize courts, and it remained uncertain whether courts in other jurisdictions, including the United States, would recognize the
as legitimate authorization to capture enemy ships and cargo.

The disruptions to Portuguese-flagged shipping hardened Portuguese resolve to mount an invasion, and Montevideo fell to Luso-Brazilian forces in January 1817, followed by Colonia. The Oriental Republic persisted as a privateering sponsor, but it became a sponsor with no major port and no functioning prize court.
zh: 船长们很快就了解到，阿蒂加斯签署的委任状具有特殊价值。联合省政府的委任状规定，私掠者只能攻击西班牙船只；阿蒂加斯的
却授权捕获葡萄牙和西班牙双方的船只，使私掠者有可能从巴西及亚洲通往葡萄牙的高利润贸易中获利。但其中也存在不利之处和危险。布宜诺斯艾利斯的捕获法庭不接受这些委任状，而其他管辖区——包括美国——的法庭，会不会承认这些
是捕获敌方船只与货物的合法授权，仍不确定。
对葡萄牙旗船航运的扰乱，强化了葡萄牙发动入侵的决心；1817年1月，蒙得维的亚落入葡萄牙—巴西军队之手，科洛尼亚随后失守。东方共和国继续支持私掠，但已成为一个没有主要港口、也没有正常运作的捕获法庭的支持者。

en: There is no question that Artigas was deploying the commissions to position himself as a head of state. He burnished the official nature of the act of issuing the commissions by producing a document called the “Reglamento del Corso,” which outlined procedures for privateers and the adjudication of prizes. In 1817, in an effort to increase privateering attacks on Portuguese shipping in the midst of the Luso-Brazilian invasion, Artigas supplied a set of blank commissions to the United States consul in Buenos Aires, Thomas Lloyd Halsey, who met with Artigas at his headquarters in Purificación. There, Artigas gave Halsey a letter for President James Monroe, composed as a message from one head of state to another.
zh: 毫无疑问，阿蒂加斯正在运用这些委任状，确立自己作为国家元首的地位。他制定一份名为“Reglamento del Corso”（《私掠条例》）的文件，概述私掠者应遵循的程序及捕获物的裁判程序，以强化颁发委任状这一行为的官方性质。1817年，在葡萄牙—巴西入侵期间，为增加针对葡萄牙船只的私掠袭击，阿蒂加斯向美国驻布宜诺斯艾利斯领事托马斯·劳埃德·哈尔西提供了一批空白委任状。哈尔西在普里菲卡西翁的总部与阿蒂加斯会面；在那里，阿蒂加斯交给他一封致詹姆斯·门罗总统的信，其写法是一个国家元首致另一个国家元首的讯息。

en: As a strategy for widening the war, the distribution of blank commissions was very effective. Between 1817 and 1820, with Artigas isolated between Luso-Brazilian invaders and the quietly hostile Buenos Aires government, commissions signed by him were circulating in Baltimore, Savannah, Norfolk, Charleston, and Providence, and cruises against Iberian shipping across the Atlantic and Caribbean were intensifying. When the U.S. government acted to restrict the entry of South American privateers into U.S. ports in 1817, some raiders began offloading booty from Portuguese-flagged vessels at sea. Others took captured ships and cargo to prize courts in the Caribbean, especially at Juan Griego and Angostura off Venezuela, to have the captures declared good prizes. No one knew with certainty whether such tactics would enable South American raiders to be treated as legitimate, licensed privateers in U.S. ports, but there was no shortage of mariners willing to assume the risk.
zh: 作为扩大战争的策略，分发空白委任状十分有效。1817至1820年，阿蒂加斯被孤立于葡萄牙—巴西入侵者与暗怀敌意的布宜诺斯艾利斯政府之间；而他签署的委任状，却在巴尔的摩、萨凡纳、诺福克、查尔斯顿和普罗维登斯流通，针对伊比利亚船只、横跨大西洋与加勒比海的劫掠巡航日益密集。1817年，美国政府采取行动，限制南美洲私掠船进入美国港口后，一些劫掠者开始在海上卸下从葡萄牙旗船夺得的战利品。另一些则把捕获的船只和货物送至加勒比海的捕获法庭，尤其是委内瑞拉一带的胡安格列戈和安戈斯图拉，以取得合法捕获物的裁定。没有人确切知道，这些策略能否让南美洲劫掠者在美国港口被当作持有合法许可的私掠者；但愿意冒险的海员从不缺乏。

en: Raids of the
zh: 的劫掠

en: As a raider, John Daniels was not a beginner. He had acquired experience in boarding and seizing ships while serving as a privateer in the War of 1812.

When peace arrived in 1814, Daniels returned to commercial trading, sailing for the merchant house of D’Arcy and Didier. Before the war, Baltimore had been in a favored position in West Indies markets. It was the nearest U.S. port for the shipment of wheat from Pennsylvania farms, and it had strong connections to French and Spanish merchant houses operating in the Caribbean. Possibly investing the dowry of his wife, Daniels built a schooner and undertook commercial voyages for D’Arcy and Didier to Haiti and France.
zh: 作为劫掠者，约翰·丹尼尔斯并非新手。他在1812年战争期间担任私掠者，积累了登船与夺船的经验。
1814年和平到来后，丹尼尔斯重返商业贸易，为D’Arcy and Didier商行航行。战前，巴尔的摩在西印度群岛市场中居于有利位置。它是将宾夕法尼亚农场小麦运出的最近美国港口，与在加勒比海经营的法国和西班牙商行联系密切。丹尼尔斯可能以妻子的嫁妆作为投资，建造了一艘纵帆船，替D’Arcy and Didier商行开展通往海地和法国的商业航行。

en: Hopeful of regaining their competitive advantage in the West Indies trade, Baltimore merchants instead found themselves confronting a crisis of profitability. In peacetime, larger-capacity British ships were moving into markets previously served by the smaller Baltimore schooners.

The pinch on profits sent Daniels and others casting around for alternatives, and news of opportunities in the South American republics arrived on cue. In late 1817, Daniels purchased a new brigantine from a Baltimore shipyard and prepared it for an extensive cruise as a privateer.
zh: 巴尔的摩商人希望重获西印度群岛贸易中的竞争优势，实际面对的却是盈利危机。和平时期，载货量更大的英国船只，进入了此前由较小的巴尔的摩纵帆船服务的市场。
利润受到挤压，促使丹尼尔斯等人四处寻找其他出路；有关南美洲共和国机会的消息，恰在此时传来。1817年末，丹尼尔斯从巴尔的摩一家造船厂购入一艘新双桅混合帆船，准备将其用于一次长途私掠巡航。

en: Daniels was attentive to the need to defend his raiding as lawful, and he began to construct a paper trail that might secure future booty. To accept a privateering commission on U.S. soil from a South American polity would have been a violation of U.S. neutrality laws.

Hiding their tracks in various ways, other Baltimore captains had already embarked on privateering cruises with commissions from South America, and Daniels probably learned about the opportunity from his contacts and peers.
His plan to sail the newly built ship, the

, to the Río de la Plata may have been intended to support the fiction that he obtained his commission outside the United States. Daniels undertook other precautions, too. He stored the ship’s extensive cache of small arms below deck and listed Tenerife as the voyage destination when the vessel set sail in March 1818. The ship’s papers named John Cox as the captain, and Daniels—no doubt to give himself plausible deniability about planning a privateering voyage in a U.S. port—traveled with additional crew members on a pilot boat to meet the ship at the White Rocks, about 9 miles outside Baltimore harbor.
zh: 丹尼尔斯很清楚，必须把自己的劫掠辩护为合法行为；他开始建立文件记录，以便保住未来的战利品。在美国领土上接受南美洲政治体的私掠委任状，会违反美国的中立法。
其他巴尔的摩船长已经以各种方式掩盖行迹，持南美洲委任状展开私掠巡航；丹尼尔斯很可能从人脉和同业那里了解到这一机会。
他打算把新造的
驶往拉普拉塔河，这可能是为了支持他在美国境外取得委任状的说辞。丹尼尔斯还采取了其他预防措施。他把船上大量轻武器藏在甲板下，并在1818年3月起航时，将特内里费列为航行目的地。船舶文件把约翰·考克斯列为船长；丹尼尔斯则与另外一些船员乘引航船，在距巴尔的摩港约9英里的白岩与该船会合——无疑是为了让自己能够有理由否认曾在美国港口策划私掠航行。

en: Once at sea, Daniels had the arms brought up and the guns mounted.
The

then sprinted, on a three-week, 5,000-mile voyage, to Buenos Aires without calling at another port. When and how Daniels obtained the Artigas commission is a mystery, and it is possible that he already possessed it when he sailed from Baltimore.

We know that in Buenos Aires, Daniels went ashore to obtain a commission from the government of the United Provinces. As further steps to support his claim that the subsequent captures were lawful, he recorded a sale and re-purchase of the
and changed its name to the
, and became a naturalized citizen of the United Provinces.

Daniels then released and rehired his crew, except for a few men who chose to stay ashore or change ships, and he added another twenty men to the ship’s roster. When officials in Buenos Aires became suspicious that Daniels had no intention of bringing prizes back to Buenos Aires, they informed him that they would send marine observers on board. Daniels slipped out of the harbor that night.
zh: 出海后，丹尼尔斯命人把武器搬上来，并装好火炮。
随后，
在三周内航行5,000英里，直抵布宜诺斯艾利斯，途中未停靠其他港口。丹尼尔斯何时、如何取得阿蒂加斯的委任状，仍是谜；他离开巴尔的摩时，可能已经持有它。
我们知道，在布宜诺斯艾利斯，丹尼尔斯上岸取得了联合省政府的委任状。为进一步支持其后续捕获合法的主张，他登记了
的一次出售和回购，将其改名为
，并归化为联合省公民。
随后，丹尼尔斯解除船员的雇佣关系，再重新雇用他们；少数人选择留在岸上或换船，而他又将二十人加入船员名册。当布宜诺斯艾利斯官员怀疑丹尼尔斯无意把捕获物带回该港时，便通知他将派海事观察员登船。丹尼尔斯当夜悄悄驶离港口。

en: Again at sea, Daniels renamed the ship
, or the

He gathered the crew and announced that he possessed two commissions—one from the United Provinces and another from the Oriental Republic—and that he intended to raid under both. A crew member later testified that Daniels showed the crew the commission from the United Provinces, but no one remembered seeing the Artigas commission. Daniels surely knew that prize courts would not approve sailing under two commissions, and perhaps for that reason he decided to abandon the commission from the United Provinces. He sent it back to Buenos Aires by way of a passing ship. In Buenos Aires, officials confiscated the deposit filed for Daniels’s ship by a U.S. merchant and declared Daniels to be a pirate.
zh: 再次出海后，丹尼尔斯将船改名为
，即

。他召集船员，宣布自己拥有两份委任状——一份来自联合省，一份来自东方共和国——并打算同时凭借两份委任状劫掠。后来一名船员作证说，丹尼尔斯向船员展示过联合省的委任状，但没有人记得见过阿蒂加斯的委任状。丹尼尔斯肯定知道，捕获法庭不会认可持两份委任状航行；或许因此，他决定放弃联合省的那份委任状，通过一艘过往船只将它送回布宜诺斯艾利斯。在布宜诺斯艾利斯，官员没收了一名美国商人为丹尼尔斯船只缴纳的保证金，并宣布丹尼尔斯为海盗。

en: In the next seven weeks, the
seized twenty-six ships.
All but one were sailing under Portuguese colors and plying the busy sea lanes connecting Brazil to Lisbon. In most cases, the crew plundered the cargo and sank the vessels.
The richest prizes came from the two most profitable segments of Portuguese Atlantic commerce. One was the
, a Portuguese-flagged merchant vessel sailing from Bombay to Lisbon with a cargo of cotton, tea, ginger, cinnamon, saltpeter, and other spices. The
seized the cargo, later valued at $90,000 by the Portuguese consul in Baltimore, and sent the ship, valued at $30,000, to Charleston, South Carolina, presumably to be sold.
A second, even richer capture was of a Portuguese vessel called the
(later referred to in U.S. courts as the
), on a voyage from Rio de Janeiro to Lisbon. The ship was carrying “Fifty Bags of Silver, Ten Bags of Gold and Silver, [and] Five Bags of Gold” valued at about $300,000.

Confident that his privateering commission would protect him from legal challenges, Daniels returned home and placed his share of the captured treasure in the Marine Bank of Baltimore. But he was underestimating how quickly and decisively the political winds in the United States had shifted against him during his months away.
zh: 接下来七周，
捕获了二十六艘船。
除一艘外，其余都悬挂葡萄牙旗帜，往来于连接巴西与里斯本的繁忙航道。多数情况下，船员抢走货物，然后将船凿沉。
最丰厚的捕获物，来自葡萄牙大西洋贸易利润最高的两个部分。其中一艘是
，一艘悬挂葡萄牙旗帜、从孟买驶往里斯本的商船，载有棉花、茶叶、生姜、肉桂、硝石及其他香料。“不可抗拒号”夺走了货物，葡萄牙驻巴尔的摩领事后来估其价值为90,000美元；并把估值30,000美元的船只送往南卡罗来纳州查尔斯顿，推测是为了出售。
另一宗更丰厚的捕获，是名为
的葡萄牙船（后来在美国法院中被称为
），当时正从里约热内卢驶往里斯本。船上载着“五十袋白银、十袋金银，以及五袋黄金”，价值约300,000美元。
丹尼尔斯相信自己的私掠委任状足以保护他免受法律挑战，便返乡将自己分得的财宝存入巴尔的摩海事银行。但他低估了自己离开这几个月间，美国的政治风向对他不利的转变有多么迅速而坚决。

en: Friendly and Unfriendly Courts
zh: 友好的法庭与不友好的法庭

en: U.S. government backing for citizens engaged in raiding for South American polities was fast eroding. Officials were facing intense lobbying by Iberian ambassadors and rapidly escalating litigation by foreign consuls.

The government was also immersed in negotiations with the Spanish government over the acquisition of Florida and other terms of what would become the Adams-Onís Treaty, and placating Spain was now a high priority for Secretary of State John Quincy Adams. Initially, Daniels responded to these dangers by quickly preparing the
for another privateering voyage.
zh: 美国政府对那些为南美洲政治体实施劫掠的本国公民的支持，正在迅速消退。官员面对着伊比利亚两国大使的强力游说，以及外国领事迅速增多的诉讼。
政府也正与西班牙就取得佛罗里达及后来构成《亚当斯—奥尼斯条约》的其他条款展开谈判；安抚西班牙，此时已成为国务卿约翰·昆西·亚当斯的重要优先事项。丹尼尔斯最初应对这些危险的方式，是迅速准备让
再度出海私掠。

en: In his second cruise, Daniels seized several dozen more ships. They included the
, a Portuguese slave ship, and a sixteen-gun Spanish warship, the brig

Daniels recognized that the ship was valuable, and he decided to take it to a prize court to have it declared good prize. He first sought a quick ruling in St. Thomas but was rebuffed by officials there. The
then accompanied the

, with a prize crew made up of Daniels’s men, to Juan Griego on the island of Margarita, where the friendly prize court would recognize his Artigas commission and award the ship to him as lawful captor.
zh: 在第二次巡航中，丹尼尔斯又捕获数十艘船。其中包括葡萄牙贩奴船
，以及装备十六门火炮的西班牙双桅横帆军舰
。丹尼尔斯意识到这艘军舰价值不菲，决定将其送往捕获法庭，取得合法捕获物的裁定。他最初希望在圣托马斯迅速获得判决，却遭当地官员拒绝。随后，
伴随由丹尼尔斯部下组成的接管船员驾驶的
，驶往玛格丽塔岛的胡安格列戈；那里的友好捕获法庭会承认他的阿蒂加斯委任状，并把船判给作为合法捕获者的他。

en: The court at Juan Griego was one of a handful of Caribbean prize courts profiting from the surge in the region’s maritime raiding. Officials in Gran Colombia had created the forum to rule on captures made by privateers sailing for the new government, and the court quickly signaled that its doors were open to captains with commissions from other Latin American states.

Following swift action by the court, Daniels conspired with his close associate Henry Childs to arrange what was likely a sham sale of the vessel to a Venezuelan citizen named Antonio Julio Franceschi. The
was rechristened the
, and the new owner—with Childs and Daniels acting in the background—secured a commission to sail as a privateer for the revolutionary government of Simón Bolívar.
zh: 胡安格列戈法庭，是从该地区海上劫掠激增中获利的少数加勒比捕获法庭之一。大哥伦比亚的官员设立这一审判机构，以裁决为新政府航行的私掠者所取得的捕获物；法庭很快便表明，它也向持有其他拉丁美洲国家委任状的船长开放。
法庭迅速作出处理后，丹尼尔斯与密切合作者亨利·查尔兹合谋，安排将该船出售给名为安东尼奥·胡利奥·弗兰切斯基的委内瑞拉公民；这很可能是一笔虚假交易。
被重新命名为
；在查尔兹和丹尼尔斯幕后操作下，新船主取得委任状，以私掠船身份为西蒙·玻利瓦尔的革命政府航行。

en: A mutiny then disrupted Daniels’s plans. The
was anchored in the harbor at Juan Griego when another Baltimore privateering vessel, the
, sailing with a commission from Buenos Aires, entered the harbor with captures of its own. The crews mingled, and with men of the
apparently in the lead, they decided to sail for home. The mutineers permitted nineteen men from the
, including Henry Childs, to go ashore. Some of those who remained would later claim they did so under duress. After rifling through the papers on the

in search of a commission and finding none, the merged crew decided to make captures without legal cover. On the way to the Chesapeake, they boarded and ransacked about thirty vessels. Like Daniels, the men discovered on their return that they were entering a political atmosphere that had turned sharply hostile to would-be privateers. Unlike Daniels, they had no claim of a commission and would not be able to argue in court that their captures were lawful acts of war. Officials rounded up crew members and put separate groups on trial for piracy in Baltimore and Richmond.
zh: 随后，一场哗变打乱了丹尼尔斯的计划。
当时停泊于胡安格列戈港，另一艘来自巴尔的摩的私掠船
，持布宜诺斯艾利斯的委任状，带着自己的捕获物进入港口。两船船员混在一起，显然在

船员带头下，决定驶船返乡。哗变者允许“不可抗拒号”上的十九人上岸，其中包括亨利·查尔兹。一些留下的人后来声称，他们是在胁迫之下留下的。合流后的船员翻遍“不可抗拒号”的文件，寻找委任状，却一无所获，于是决定在没有法律掩护的情况下实施捕获。在前往切萨皮克的途中，他们登上并洗劫了约三十艘船。与丹尼尔斯一样，这些人返乡时发现，自己进入了一种对有意从事私掠者极端敌视的政治氛围。与丹尼尔斯不同的是，他们无法声称持有委任状，也无法在法庭上主张其捕获是合法战争行为。官员将船员搜捕归案，分批在巴尔的摩和里士满以海盗罪审判。

en: Daniels managed to take advantage even of this calamity. After the mutiny at Juan Griego, he commandeered the
(the renamed
) in pursuit of the
and the mutineers. Arriving in Baltimore, he learned that the

was docked in Nottingham and that many of the mutineers were under arrest in Richmond. Daniels traveled to retrieve the ship, and port officials readily gave it to him. Once again, he found himself in possession of the
, and now he also had command of the rechristened
Yet Daniels’s position had never been less secure, and he found himself badly in need of a lawyer.
zh: 即便这场灾难，丹尼尔斯也设法加以利用。胡安格列戈哗变之后，他征用了
，即改名后的
，追赶
和哗变者。抵达巴尔的摩后，他得知“不可抗拒号”停在诺丁汉，许多哗变者已在里士满被捕。丹尼尔斯前往取船，港口官员爽快地把船交还给他。他再次拥有了“不可抗拒号”，如今还指挥着改名后的
。然而，丹尼尔斯的地位从未如此不稳固，他发现自己急需一名律师。

en: He was facing three claims, called libels, to recover captured ships and cargo. The Portuguese consul to the United States, Joaquim José Vasques, had sued for the return of the treasure of the
The Portuguese consul in Maryland, William Swift, presented a libel on behalf of the Portuguese crown to recover the value of goods seized from the
and twenty-five other vessels on the first cruise of the
And the Spanish consul in Baltimore, Juan Bautista Bernabeu, demanded that Daniels return the
to the Spanish government. The cases appeared before Theodorick Bland, a Maryland judge known for his support of South American revolutions and at one time suspected of involvement in privateering.
The cases would spotlight the shifting contours of the emerging Atlantic system by generating debates over the definition of states, war, and piracy.
zh: 他正面对三项要求追回被捕船只及货物的诉请，这类诉状称为libels。葡萄牙驻美国领事若阿金·若泽·瓦斯克斯，起诉要求归还
的财宝。葡萄牙驻马里兰州领事威廉·斯威夫特，代表葡萄牙王室提交诉状，要求追回
第一次巡航中，从
及另外二十五艘船上夺取的货物价值。西班牙驻巴尔的摩领事胡安·包蒂斯塔·贝尔纳贝乌，则要求丹尼尔斯向西班牙政府归还
。这些案件由马里兰州法官西奥多里克·布兰德审理；他以支持南美洲革命闻名，一度还被怀疑参与私掠。
这些案件围绕国家、战争和海盗行为的定义引发辩论，使正在形成的大西洋体系不断变化的轮廓凸显出来。

en: What is a State?
zh: 什么是国家？

en: The dispute over the capture of the
was on one level straightforward. The case ultimately turned on the question of whether Daniels had violated U.S. neutrality laws by fitting out the ship for war in Baltimore.

As judge in the district court, Bland declared himself unconvinced by Daniels’s claim that the ship had been on a commercial voyage before obtaining a privateering commission in the Río de la Plata. The ship had been prepared for war in Baltimore, Bland found, ruling that Daniels had to return the rich booty from the

His judgment was affirmed on appeal in the circuit court of Maryland. The case next reached the U.S. Supreme Court, where Chief Justice John Marshall pronounced himself certain, too, that “there was no commercial voyage.” Even if the crew had not been formally contracted to join a raiding expedition, Marshall concluded, “Every thing they saw, every thing that was done, spoke a language too plain to be misunderstood.” Daniels had organized—in a port in the United States—a piratical voyage, and nothing that occurred in the Río de la Plata had removed that taint.
zh: 围绕捕获
的争议，在一个层面上十分直接。案件最终取决于这样一个问题：丹尼尔斯在巴尔的摩将船只装备为战船，是否违反了美国中立法。
作为地区法院法官，布兰德表示，他不相信丹尼尔斯的说法，即该船在拉普拉塔河取得私掠委任状之前，一直从事商业航行。布兰德认定，该船在巴尔的摩就已为战争作好准备，因此判令丹尼尔斯归还从
取得的丰厚战利品。他的判决，在马里兰巡回法院上诉审中获得维持。案件随后提交美国最高法院，首席大法官约翰·马歇尔同样表示确信：“根本没有商业航行。”马歇尔认为，即使船员未正式签约参加劫掠远征，“他们看到的每一件事，所做的每一件事，都表达着明白到不可能误解的意思”。丹尼尔斯在美国港口组织了一次海盗航行，而拉普拉塔河发生的任何事情，都未消除这一污点。

en: The

case also prompted wide-ranging debates about the sovereignty of South American governments. Appearing for the Portuguese crown, David Hoffman argued that Daniels could not have been acting as a privateer because “the Banda Oriental is not a state or nation invested with the attributes of sovereignty.” Nor had the U.S. government “recognized Artigas as engaged in a civil war with Spain, or in a war of any kind with Portugal.” Going still further, Hoffman proposed that recognizing Artigas as a head of state would disrupt the entire region: “If Artigas, and his wretched and savage followers be recognized as qualified to wage

, then may every township, district, city, village, hamlet, or individual, claim the same high prerogatives.” The Banda Oriental also could not be a state, Hoffman argued, because it did not look or act the part. A state had to possess a “fixed
, a
, a
, a
,” and to make war by sea it needed to have seaports. Hoffman asserted that even if Artigas governed as if he were a head of state, he would remain the leader of only a “horde of men.”
zh: 案还引发了有关南美洲政府主权的广泛辩论。代表葡萄牙王室出庭的戴维·霍夫曼主张，丹尼尔斯不可能是在以私掠者身份行动，因为“东岸地区并非具有主权属性的国家或民族国家”。美国政府也未“承认阿蒂加斯正与西班牙进行内战，或与葡萄牙进行任何形式的战争”。霍夫曼更进一步提出，承认阿蒂加斯为国家元首，会扰乱整个地区：“如果阿蒂加斯及其卑劣而野蛮的追随者，被承认为有资格发动
，那么每一个乡镇、地区、城市、村庄、小聚落，乃至个人，都可以主张同样的崇高特权。”霍夫曼还主张，东岸地区不可能是国家，因为它在外观和行为上都不像国家。国家必须拥有“固定的
”；要在海上作战，还必须拥有海港。霍夫曼断言，即使阿蒂加斯以国家元首的方式治理，他仍然只是“一群乌合之众”的首领。

en: The possibility that the U.S. government might have already indicated that the Oriental Republic was sovereign lurked in the background. Hoffman acknowledged that in Monroe’s second address to Congress on 17 November 1818, the president had stated, “It appears … that the government of Buenos Ayres declared itself independent in July, 1816 … [and] that the Banda Oriental, Entre Rios, and Paraguay, with the city of Santa Fe, all of which
, are unconnected with the present government of Buenos Ayres.”
Hoffman could not ignore Monroe’s statement. But he suggested that the president had recognized only some aspects of sovereignty in the Banda Oriental and not “the high privileges of sovereignty.”
zh: 美国政府可能已经表明东方共和国具有主权，这一可能性始终隐伏于争论背后。霍夫曼承认，门罗在1818年11月17日第二次向国会发表咨文时曾说：“看来……布宜诺斯艾利斯政府已于1816年7月宣布独立……而东岸地区、恩特雷里奥斯和巴拉圭，以及圣菲市，都
，与目前的布宜诺斯艾利斯政府没有联系。”
霍夫曼无法忽视门罗的表述，但他提出，总统只是承认了东岸地区主权的某些方面，而非“主权的崇高特权”。

en: The crux of this argument was that former colonies possessed only a limited capacity to make war. Hoffman reasoned that a colony recognized by other governments as “engaged in a civil war for the assertion of its independence” might oppose only “the parent country and its allies.” It could not “wage a distinct, and independent war with other nations.” Under this logic, the Banda Oriental was something other than a state among states, having been awarded only “limited and partial” recognition by the United States. The courts could not remedy this situation because they lacked the authority “to declare that a people
a state … [or] that they
a state.”
zh: 这一论证的关键，是原殖民地仅拥有有限的战争能力。霍夫曼推论，一个被其他政府承认为“正为争取独立而进行内战”的殖民地，只能对抗“母国及其盟友”，不能“与其他国家发动另一场独立的战争”。按照这一逻辑，东岸地区并非与其他国家并列的国家，因为美国只给予它“有限而部分”的承认。法院无法补救这一局面，因为它没有权力“宣布一个人民
国家……或宣布他们
一个国家”。

en: In reply, Daniels’s attorney, William Winder, asserted that “the Banda Oriental was a sovereign state
” Winder was echoing arguments he had made in the case of the

, a case that turned on whether a ship’s crew had been augmented illegally in Norfolk, Virginia, before making captures. In that case, Winder had described the act of issuing privateering commissions as “the very highest act of sovereignty” and therefore “peculiarly above ordinary judicial control in foreign countries.” A state at war was by definition a sovereign state; it could not be restricted to making war only to the degree that neutral tribunals would permit.
zh: 作为回应，丹尼尔斯的律师威廉·温德断言：“东岸地区是一个
主权国家。”温德重申了他在
案中提出的论证；该案取决于船只实施捕获前，是否曾在弗吉尼亚州诺福克非法扩充船员。在那个案件中，温德把颁发私掠委任状称为“最高层次的主权行为”，因而“尤其超出外国普通司法控制的范围”。交战国家依定义就是主权国家；其作战程度，不能被限制在中立法庭所允许的范围内。

en: These arguments spilled beyond the courtroom. As the cases involving Daniels and other captains moved through the system, Iberian diplomats were pressuring U.S. officials to do more to rein in privateering from U.S. ports. Not surprisingly, their arguments echoed those of the lawyers hired and directed by Iberian consuls. In March 1819, the Portuguese ambassador, José Corrêa da Serra, visited John Quincy Adams to demand (in “crippled English,” Adams noted privately) that the government declare all captains and crews sailing on ships with commissions from Artigas to be pirates. The ambassador was fixated on Artigas’s lack of seaports under his command. Corrêa da Serra urged Adams to imagine his reaction if privateers attacked U.S. citizens and their property “under the flag and Commission of Tecumseh.”

The complaint added to one months before in which Corrêa da Serra railed that “privateering Commissions from Artigas were mere absurdities” and carried as much weight as commissions “from the Seminole Indians.”
zh: 这些论证溢出了法庭。当涉及丹尼尔斯及其他船长的案件在司法体系中推进时，伊比利亚两国外交官正在向美国官员施压，要求采取更多措施，遏制从美国港口出发的私掠。毫不意外，他们的论点与由两国领事雇用、指挥的律师的论点彼此呼应。1819年3月，葡萄牙大使若泽·科雷亚·达塞拉拜访约翰·昆西·亚当斯，要求政府宣布，所有乘持有阿蒂加斯委任状船只航行的船长和船员，都是海盗（亚当斯私下记下，大使使用的是“蹩脚的英语”）。大使紧盯着阿蒂加斯控制下没有海港这一点。科雷亚·达塞拉敦促亚当斯设想：如果私掠者“在特库姆塞的旗帜与委任状之下”袭击美国公民及其财产，他会作何反应？
几个月前，科雷亚·达塞拉已作过类似抱怨，怒斥“阿蒂加斯颁发的私掠委任状纯属荒谬”，其效力与“塞米诺尔印第安人”颁发的委任状相同。

en: Although in making these analogies Corrêa da Serra was focusing on Artigas’s lack of access to ports, the comparisons to Native American polities were hardly casual. Floating phrases such as “limited and partial recognition” and “

statehood” and debating the kinds of wars that former colonies could legitimately wage, advocates in privateering disputes were grasping at ways to situate some political communities in an in-between, unsettled status. It would be another fifteen years before Chief Justice Marshall would characterize the Native American polities as “domestic dependent nations.”

There was nothing approaching a settled vocabulary to draw on to describe quasi-sovereignty, sovereign indeterminacy, or incompletely recognized states. The ambiguities left South American governments in a bind. By issuing privateering commissions, they were asserting the right of sovereigns to make war but exposing themselves to accusations of sponsoring piracy.
zh: 尽管科雷亚·达塞拉作这些类比时，重点是阿蒂加斯无法使用海港，但与美洲原住民政治体的比较绝非随意。私掠纠纷中的辩护者提出“有限而部分的承认”和“
国家地位”等说法，并争论原殖民地可以合法发动哪些战争，其实是在摸索如何把某些政治共同体置于一种介于其间、尚未确定的地位。还要过十五年，首席大法官马歇尔才会把美洲原住民政治体称为“国内依附民族”。
当时，远没有一套固定词汇，可以用来描述准主权、主权的不确定性或未获完整承认的国家。这些含混使南美洲政府陷入两难：颁发私掠委任状，一方面是在主张主权者发动战争的权利，另一方面也使自己暴露于支持海盗的指控之下。

en: What is War?
zh: 什么是战争？

en: The link between state status and rights to make war featured prominently in the second major suit against Daniels, the case of the
As in the
case, there was strong evidence that Daniels had violated U.S. neutrality laws. In support of the libel by the Spanish consul to recover the
, two seamen from the
confirmed that the ship had left Baltimore carrying arms below deck and fifty or sixty men—more than a typical crew for a commercial voyage.
But the case had another element, one that led Judge Theodorick Bland to rule in favor of Daniels. A prize crew from the
had taken the
to the court at Juan Griego, where it was declared a lawful prize. Daniels’s associate Henry Childs gave detailed testimony about the court proceedings and the sale of the
to the Venezuelan citizen Franceschi.
zh: 国家地位与战争权利之间的联系，在针对丹尼尔斯的第二起重大诉讼——
案——中尤其突出。与
案一样，有强有力的证据表明，丹尼尔斯违反了美国中立法。为支持西班牙领事要求追回
的诉请，“不可抗拒号”上的两名海员证实，该船离开巴尔的摩时，甲板下藏有武器，船上有五六十人，超过一般商业航行所需的船员数量。
但案件还有另一因素，促使西奥多里克·布兰德法官作出有利于丹尼尔斯的判决。“不可抗拒号”的接管船员已将
送往胡安格列戈法庭，在那里，该船被判为合法捕获物。丹尼尔斯的合作者亨利·查尔兹，详细作证说明了法庭程序，以及把
出售给委内瑞拉公民弗兰切斯基的情况。

en: Bland backed Daniels. He began by affirming that the

had been outfitted for war in Baltimore in violation of the neutrality act. But, Bland continued, the case before him was not about Daniels’s criminal responsibility, it was about the “seizure by a lawfully commissioned cruiser of a belligerent.” Bland acknowledged widespread uncertainty about the status of nations “born at once” in the southern Atlantic and “the station they were to be allowed to assume” according to “the older nations of the earth.” He regarded these questions as “generally rather political than legal.” Civil war was still a kind of war, Bland observed. If a neutral nation declared a conflict to be a civil war, “its courts cannot consider as criminal those acts of hostility, which war authorizes.”
zh: 布兰德支持丹尼尔斯。他首先确认，“不可抗拒号”在巴尔的摩被装备为战船，违反了中立法。但布兰德接着说，他面前的案件并非有关丹尼尔斯的刑事责任，而是有关“一艘获得合法委任的交战方巡航舰所实施的捕获”。布兰德承认，对于南大西洋那些“同时诞生”的国家的地位，以及依“地球上较古老国家”的看法应允许它们取得何种“位置”，普遍存在不确定性。他认为，这些问题“总体而言，与其说是法律性的，不如说是政治性的”。布兰德指出，内战仍是一种战争。如果一个中立国家宣布某场冲突为内战，“其法院便不能把战争所许可的敌对行为视为犯罪”。

en: Like the lawyers on both sides of the

case, Bland parsed Monroe’s presidential messages about South American states. He noted that on 2 December 1817, Monroe had declared that the former colonies of Spain were not engaged in an “ordinary insurrection or rebellion” but in a “civil war between parties nearly equal.” Bland quoted Monroe’s second address to Congress in November 1818, in which he named the Banda Oriental as “independent,” and he cited the president’s message of 17 December 1819, which affirmed that U.S. ports were “equally open to both parties.” Monroe had commented that Buenos Aires was steadily maintaining its claim to independence, alongside “the Provinces north of the La Plata bordering on it.” Bland concluded that the president had clearly “designated that country of which José Artigas is the Chief, as one capable of having a maritime force, and as conveniently situated for such a force.” The executive had also explicitly recognized a “civil war between that country and Spain.”
zh: 与

案双方律师一样，布兰德细读了门罗有关南美洲国家的总统咨文。他指出，1817年12月2日，门罗曾宣布，西班牙的原殖民地并非处于“普通的暴动或叛乱”之中，而是在进行一场“双方力量大致相当的内战”。布兰德引用了门罗1818年11月第二次向国会发表的咨文，其中将东岸地区称为“独立”；又引用总统1819年12月17日的咨文，其中确认美国港口“向双方同等开放”。门罗曾说，布宜诺斯艾利斯正与“拉普拉塔河以北、与之接壤的诸省”一道，稳步坚持其独立主张。布兰德得出结论，总统显然“把何塞·阿蒂加斯担任首领的那个国家，确定为能够拥有海上武装、且地理位置适合拥有这种武装的国家”。行政当局也明确承认“该国与西班牙之间存在内战”。

en: Bland now turned to the question of the relationship between the Banda Oriental and Venezuela. President Monroe, he asserted, had identified only “two parties in the civil war, ‘Spain and the Colonies.’” With a confidence that would irk Justice Story when the case arrived on appeal at the Supreme Court, Bland stated without qualification that “the Executive has distinctly recognized those two governments of the Banda Oriental, and of Venezuela as cobelligerents, associates, companions, and allies in the war against Spain.” According to the law of nations, Bland continued, captures by an authorized belligerent’s vessel, even one “illegally fitted out” in the ports of a neutral, were valid. He concluded, “There can be no doubt that the commission of the Irresistible from the government of the Oriental Republic was legal.” On appeal, the circuit court of Maryland affirmed Bland’s ruling that the
did not have to be restored to the Spanish government.
zh: 布兰德随后转向东岸地区与委内瑞拉的关系问题。他断言，门罗总统只识别出“内战中的两方：‘西班牙与殖民地’”。布兰德毫不保留地说：“行政当局已明确承认，东岸地区与委内瑞拉这两个政府，是对西班牙战争中的共同交战方、伙伴、同伴和盟友。”当案件上诉至最高法院时，这种笃定令斯托里大法官恼火。布兰德继续说，依照万国法，经授权的交战方船只所实施的捕获，即使该船曾在中立国港口“非法装备”，也仍然有效。他总结道：“毫无疑问，东方共和国政府颁发给不可抗拒号的委任状是合法的。”在上诉中，马里兰巡回法院维持了布兰德的判决，即
无须归还西班牙政府。

en: When the case reached the Supreme Court, lawyers for the Spanish side tried a new tactic, heaping doubt on the jurisdiction and proceedings of the prize court at Juan Griego and asserting an expansive authority of U.S. courts to evaluate foreign prize proceedings.

They began by asserting that there was “no evidence whatever of an alliance between Venezuela and the Banda Oriental.” Even though Monroe had acknowledged that the Banda Oriental and Venezuela were “at war with Spain,” it did not necessarily follow that they were allies—or even engaged in the same war. Nor was Monroe’s statement “sufficient to authorize the Court to allow to Artigas all the rights of war.”

Going further, attorneys for Spain proposed that even if Venezuela was recognized as fully independent, its law could not be held to contradict that of the United States since “all sovereignty is, in its nature, as a general rule, local.” U.S. courts’ jurisdiction derived from the principle that a foreign prize court’s proceedings were “always open to inquiry” and its acts could always be nullified by another power.
zh: 案件提交最高法院后，西班牙一方的律师尝试新策略，对胡安格列戈捕获法庭的管辖权及其程序提出重重质疑，并主张美国法院拥有广泛权力，可以评判外国捕获程序。
他们首先宣称，“没有任何证据表明委内瑞拉与东岸地区之间存在联盟”。即便门罗承认东岸地区与委内瑞拉都“在同西班牙交战”，也不必然意味着它们是盟友，甚至不意味着它们在进行同一场战争。门罗的表述，也“不足以授权法院赋予阿蒂加斯全部战争权利”。
西班牙的代理律师进一步提出，即使委内瑞拉被承认为完全独立，其法律也不能被认为可以抵触美国法律，因为“一切主权，从其性质来说，作为一般规则，都是地方性的”。美国法院的管辖权源自这一原则：外国捕获法庭的程序“始终可以被审查”，其行为始终可以被另一国权力机关宣告无效。

en: Justice Story sidestepped these issues in ordering the return of the

to Spain. His ruling focused on the fact that Daniels had not produced documents from the court at Juan Griego. The failure to respond to the court’s order to do so, Story asserted, created suspicion “as to the whole transaction.” Story also credited evidence that the sale to Franceschi had been a ruse, citing Franceschi’s absence in U.S. proceedings and Daniels’s exclusive management of the ship after its arrival in the United States. Implicitly, Story’s ruling affirmed the court’s authority to question foreign prize court proceedings.
zh: 斯托里大法官在命令向西班牙归还
时，避开了这些问题。他的裁决聚焦于丹尼尔斯未能提供胡安格列戈法庭文件这一事实。斯托里断言，不遵从法院要求提交文件的命令，使“整个交易”都蒙上疑点。斯托里也采信了出售给弗兰切斯基只是骗局的证据，指出弗兰切斯基未出席美国的诉讼程序，而且该船抵达美国后，完全由丹尼尔斯管理。斯托里的裁决，隐含地确认了该院质疑外国捕获法庭程序的权力。

en: Like arguments about the capture of the

, the positions taken in the Nereyda case reveal the political stakes of unresolved questions in the campaign against South American privateering. Advocates interpreted statements by the U.S. president about the sovereignty of South American polities in ways that laid bare the ambiguities of their status. Lawyers representing foreign claimants referred to “partial recognition,” ascribed limited sovereignty to former colonies, and warned of the harm to neutrals of unbridled raiding. In the

case, arguments centered on whether South American polities were at war or in a civil war ignited by rebellion. The debates planted doubts not just about the legitimacy of Daniels’s sponsor but also about the relationships among insurgent governments and the composition of the Atlantic order.
zh: 与围绕捕获
的论证一样，Nereyda号案中的各方立场，揭示了在打击南美洲私掠的行动中，那些悬而未决的问题所涉及的政治利害。辩护者以不同方式解释美国总统关于南美洲政治体主权的表述，暴露了这些政治体地位的含混。代表外国权利主张者的律师援引“部分承认”，把有限主权赋予原殖民地，并警告不受约束的劫掠会伤害中立方。在
案中，论证集中于：南美洲政治体是在进行战争，还是在进行由叛乱引发的内战。这些辩论不仅对丹尼尔斯支持者的合法性埋下疑问，也对各起义政府之间的关系，以及大西洋秩序的构成，埋下疑问。

en: What is a Pirate?
zh: 什么是海盗？

en: Daniels’s legal jeopardy did not end with these cases. A third suit was brought—and won—for the recovery of the booty seized from the
and twenty-five other Portuguese ships.
Daniels also faced criminal charges. One indictment was sparked by the two leaders of the

mutiny, who accused Daniels of the murder of a British captain during the ship’s second cruise, when shots were fired on a British merchant vessel after it had lowered its flag. This case, too, came before Judge Bland, who cited the fog of war and acquitted Daniels of intentionally causing the captain’s death. The second set of charges formed part of a response in Baltimore to pressures from Washington officials to curtail South American privateering. Daniels was tried for violating the neutrality act. Theodorick Bland again acquitted Daniels, reasoning in part that the captain had acted outside the period covered by the latest revision of the neutrality act. To a frustrated John Quincy Adams, the verdict was based on “a legal quibble,” an example of a cramped “Law-Logic—an artificial system of reasoning, exclusively used in Courts of Justice, but good for nothing any where else.”
zh: 这些案件并未终结丹尼尔斯的法律风险。第三起诉讼要求追回从
及另外二十五艘葡萄牙船上夺得的战利品，并获得胜诉。

丹尼尔斯还面对刑事指控。其中一项起诉由“不可抗拒号”哗变的两位头目引发，他们指控丹尼尔斯在该船第二次巡航中谋杀一位英国船长：一艘英国商船降旗之后，仍遭到开火。此案也由布兰德法官审理；他援引战争中的混乱，判丹尼尔斯并未故意造成该船长死亡。另一组指控，则是巴尔的摩回应华盛顿官员施压、要求限制南美洲私掠行动的一部分。丹尼尔斯因违反中立法受审。西奥多里克·布兰德再次宣告丹尼尔斯无罪，部分理由是船长行动的时间，不在最新版中立法所涵盖的时期内。沮丧的约翰·昆西·亚当斯认为，这一判决建立在“法律上的诡辩”之上，体现了一种狭隘的“法律逻辑——一套人为的推理系统，专用于法院，在其他任何地方都毫无用处”。

en: If Daniels escaped punishment, some crew members of the
were not so lucky. Seven mutineers were tried in Baltimore for piracy, and nineteen others were tried in Richmond in July 1819.

(named for Thomas Smith, one of the ringleaders) was heard in the circuit court of Virginia, with Chief Justice Marshall serving as one of two justices on circuit, and presented at the U.S. Supreme Court before Justice Joseph Story and Justice Henry Brockholst Livingston. Two influential lawyers argued the case, Attorney General William Wirt for the government and Daniel Webster for the accused.
zh: 丹尼尔斯逃过了惩罚，但
的一些船员没有这么幸运。七名哗变者在巴尔的摩因海盗罪受审，另有十九人于1819年7月在里士满受审。
，以头目之一托马斯·史密斯命名，在弗吉尼亚巡回法院审理，首席大法官马歇尔作为两位巡回审判法官之一参与审判；该案又提交美国最高法院，由约瑟夫·斯托里大法官和亨利·布罗克霍尔斯特·利文斯顿大法官审理。两位颇具影响力的律师在该案中辩论：司法部长威廉·沃特代表政府，丹尼尔·韦伯斯特代表被告。

en: The piracy case unfolded against the background of efforts to strengthen laws to contain raiding. Faced with the surge in privateering involving U.S. citizens, Congress passed legislation in March 1819—only a month before the return of Daniels and the crew of the
to U.S. ports—to widen the definition of piracy.
The act established that anyone on the high seas who committed “the crime of piracy,

children: as defined by the law of nations

en: ” could be “punished with death” if convicted.
It did not specify how the courts would determine the definition of piracy under the law of nations.
zh: 这起海盗案展开时，当局正致力于强化法律，以遏制劫掠。面对涉及美国公民的私掠激增，国会于1819年3月通过立法，扩大海盗罪的定义；这距丹尼尔斯与
船员返回美国港口，仅有一个月。
该法令规定，任何人在公海上犯下“
海盗罪”，一经定罪，可以“处以死刑”。
法令未具体说明，法院应如何确定万国法之下海盗罪的定义。

en: The criminal case against the mutinous crew of the
tested interpretations of the piracy statute.
The jury had no trouble reaching the conclusion that the mutineers had seized the

at Juan Griego and “proceeded to sea on a cruize, without any documents of commission whatever.” They also found that the crew had captured and plundered a Spanish vessel, as charged. But jurors could not decide whether such an act amounted to piracy under the law. With Marshall’s encouragement, they issued a special verdict: “If the plunder and robbery aforesaid be piracy under the act of the Congress of the United States … then we find the said prisoner guilty; if the plunder and robbery, above stated, be not piracy under the said act of Congress then we find him, not guilty.”
The question that baffled the jury and divided the judges was whether the defendants had committed piracy under the law of nations and could therefore be punished under the act of Congress.
zh: 针对
哗变船员的刑事案件，检验了对海盗罪法规的解释。
陪审团毫不困难地得出结论：哗变者在胡安格列戈夺取“不可抗拒号”，随后“出海巡航，没有任何委任文件”。他们也认定，船员确如指控所言，捕获并洗劫了一艘西班牙船。但陪审员无法确定，这种行为在法律上是否构成海盗罪。在马歇尔鼓励下，他们作出特别裁决：“如果上述掠夺与抢劫，依照美国国会法令……构成海盗罪，那么我们认定该被告有罪；如果上述掠夺与抢劫，依照该国会法令不构成海盗罪，那么我们认定他无罪。”
使陪审团困惑、并令法官产生分歧的问题，是被告是否犯下万国法之下的海盗罪，因而可以依国会法令受到惩罚。

en: Attorney General William Wirt declared that there was no mystery. All “writers on the public law,” he stated, agreed that piracy was “depredation on the seas, without the authority of a commission, or beyond its authority.” The definition was “certain, consistent, and unanimous.” Wirt reasoned that since all nations could try and punish pirates as
, it followed that piracy’s definition was securely rooted in the law of nations.
Daniel Webster countered that there was no fixed definition of piracy among writers on public law. The purpose of the act was in fact to make Congress responsible for resolving this question.
zh: 司法部长威廉·沃特宣称，此事毫无神秘之处。他说，所有“公法著作家”都认同，海盗行为是“在海上实施劫掠，未获委任状授权，或超出其授权范围”。这一定义是“确定、一致且无异议的”。沃特推论，既然所有国家都可以把海盗作为
（全人类之敌）审判和惩罚，那么海盗罪的定义，必然牢固地扎根于万国法。
丹尼尔·韦伯斯特反驳说，公法著作家之间并无固定的海盗罪定义。该法令的目的，实际上是让国会负责解决这一问题。

en: In the Supreme Court, Justice Story agreed with Wirt that there was broad consensus among writers on the law of nations that piracy was robbery at sea outside a state of war. It was “the general practice of all nations” to punish such actions, a pattern that amounted to “conclusive proof” that the definition need not rest on “particular provisions of the municipal code, but upon the law of nations.”

In dissent, Livingston echoed concerns raised in the circuit court by Marshall that piracy was punishable only as it was defined under domestic law. The burden was on Congress, Livingston argued, “to select from sources … and then to declare, and with reasonable precision to define, what act or acts should constitute this crime.”
Piracy was not like murder or robbery—crimes in every state of the union for which “no one is allowed to allege his ignorance.”

Citizens were not so familiar with the law of nations. Further, Livingston observed, it would be unjust to declare “that all offences against the law of nations, without defining any one of them, should be punished
zh: 在最高法院，斯托里大法官同意沃特的说法：万国法著作家广泛认同，海盗行为是战争状态之外的海上抢劫。惩罚此类行为，是“所有国家的一般实践”；这种模式构成“决定性证据”，表明其定义无须建立在“国内法典的特定条款之上，而应建立在万国法之上”。
利文斯顿在异议意见中，呼应了马歇尔在巡回法院提出的忧虑：只有依国内法所定义的海盗行为，才能受到惩罚。利文斯顿认为，责任在于国会，“从各项来源中选择……然后宣布，并以合理的精确程度界定，何种或哪些行为构成这一罪行”。
海盗罪不同于谋杀或抢劫；后两者在联邦各州都是犯罪，“任何人都不得以不知法为由辩解”。
公民对万国法并没有那么熟悉。利文斯顿进一步指出，如果宣布“一切违反万国法的行为，无须定义其中任何一种，都应
”，那将是不公正的。

en: Despite the court’s affirmation of their guilt, the men did not hang. Responding to pressures from port cities for leniency, the government pardoned two men and issued a reprieve for the others.

The calls for mercy highlighted the fact that the mutineers’ crimes had not been very violent. The defense presented testimony that the piratical crew had treated its victims gently and profited only slightly from their predations. One crew member testified he was an unwilling participant who had not been able to get to shore after the

was seized in Juan Griego. The press, the jury, and even some judges found it difficult to equate an act of small violence by members of settled port communities with the imagination of unfettered violence by enemies of all.
zh: 尽管法院确认他们有罪，这些人并未被绞死。面对港口城市要求宽大处理的压力，政府赦免两人，并对其余人暂缓执行刑罚。
请求宽恕的呼声强调，哗变者的犯罪并没有很强的暴力性。辩方提出证词，称这些海盗船员温和地对待受害者，从劫掠中获利也很有限。一名船员作证说，自己是不情愿的参与者，在“不可抗拒号”于胡安格列戈被夺取后，未能上岸。报界、陪审团，甚至某些法官，都难以将定居港口社群成员实施的小规模暴力，与想象中“所有人的敌人”不受约束的暴力等同起来。

en: It is doubtful that the case against the
and
mutineers was, as one scholar claims, the “most important piracy case” in U.S. history and had “a profound effect on the development of international law in the United States.”
The case did simplify U.S. courts’ approach to piracy cases by affirming that the law of nations could be incorporated, without elaboration, in a U.S. criminal statute.
But the ruling merely shifted from Congress to the courts the burden of developing a body of law on which to rely in characterizing the law of nations.

In that task, Story’s opinion was of questionable help. His seventeen-page footnote on definitions of piracy showed that legal writers recognized piracy as a crime under the law of nations, but it did not describe other aspects of “the general practice of all nations” nor specify the connections to piracy under the common law.

As Rubin notes, the approach left open the possibility that the label of “piracy” might be used “to condemn whatever crimes the municipal law system of the United States wanted to attach to the label.”
zh: 有学者声称，针对
与
哗变者的案件，是美国历史上“最重要的海盗案”，并“对国际法在美国的发展产生深远影响”；这一说法值得怀疑。
该案确实简化了美国法院处理海盗案件的方式，因为它确认，万国法可以不经详细阐释，直接被纳入美国刑事法规。
但这一判决只是把责任从国会转移给法院：后者必须发展出一套法律，以便在界定万国法时有所依据。
在这一任务上，斯托里的意见能提供多少帮助，颇有疑问。他那长达十七页、讨论海盗定义的脚注表明，法律著作家承认海盗是万国法之下的犯罪，却没有描述“所有国家的一般实践”的其他方面，也未说明它与普通法下海盗罪的联系。
正如鲁宾所言，这种路径留下了一种可能：“海盗”标签可以被用来“谴责美国国内法体系想要附加在这一标签之下的任何罪行”。

en: States without Recognition
zh: 未获承认的国家

en: As the cases arising from the raids of the

were moving through U.S. courts, questions about which entities would gain recognition as states were playing out in an intricate politics of recognition on both sides of the Atlantic. Leaders of new and emerging polities angled to position their states in the international order by demonstrating their sovereignty.
Established empire-states assembled ad hoc policies of recognition that officials hoped would not jeopardize imperial interests or destabilize existing alliances.
zh: 当由
劫掠引发的案件在美国法院中推进时，哪些实体将获得国家承认的问题，也在大西洋两岸复杂的承认政治中展开。新生和正在形成的政治体的领导人，设法通过展示主权，确立其国家在国际秩序中的位置。
既有的帝国国家则拼合出权宜性的承认政策，官员希望这些政策既不损害帝国利益，也不动摇现有联盟。

en: The transition from a collection of political experiments to a regional system of states gained momentum when, in 1822, the U.S. government recognized five new nations: the United Provinces, Chile, Gran Colombia, Peru, and Mexico.

Britain soon followed suit, taking steps toward partial recognition by dispatching consuls to South America in 1823 and beginning negotiations on commercial treaties, then recognizing the United Provinces, Colombia, Mexico, and Brazil in 1825.
Behind these events lay a complex imperial project to guide regional political change through a combination of diplomacy and legal maneuvering, delivered through prize litigation and port politics.
zh: 1822年，美国政府承认五个新国家——联合省、智利、大哥伦比亚、秘鲁和墨西哥——使从一系列政治试验转向区域国家体系的过程获得动力。
英国很快跟进：1823年向南美洲派遣领事，并开始商业条约谈判，迈出部分承认的步骤；随后于1825年承认联合省、哥伦比亚、墨西哥和巴西。
这些事件背后，是一项复杂的帝国计划，试图通过外交与法律操作相结合，引导地区政治变化；这一计划经由捕获物诉讼与港口政治付诸实施。

en: Consider the Spanish reaction to U.S. privateering. Spanish consuls in U.S. ports devotedly gathered information about privateering activities and organized legal action. They also flooded the Spanish ambassador’s office with reports of captures of Spanish ships and complaints about the audacity of captains and crews returning to U.S. cities without fear of consequences for rampant raiding. The correspondence of Juan Bautista Bernabeu, the Spanish consul in Baltimore between 1795 and 1821, reveals the scope and energy of this consular activism.

Bernabeu’s early reports listed the comings and goings of Spanish vessels in the harbor, recorded disease outbreaks, and passed along snippets of local news. In the final five years of his tenure, Bernabeu’s attention was almost entirely absorbed by privateering—or piracy, as Spanish officials described U.S. mariners’ raiding. He sent detailed, sometimes daily missives to the Spanish ambassador and hectored him about funds needed to pay lawyers to represent the Spanish government in privateering cases and support Spanish mariners arriving in Baltimore who had been serving on crews of captured vessels. He described in minute detail the progress of the numerous legal challenges he was sponsoring for the recovery of Spanish property.
zh: 不妨考察西班牙对美国私掠的反应。西班牙驻美国港口的领事，积极搜集私掠活动的情报，并组织法律行动。他们也向西班牙大使办公室大量报送西班牙船只被捕获的消息，抱怨船长和船员肆意劫掠后，竟敢返回美国城市，毫不担心承担后果。1795至1821年任西班牙驻巴尔的摩领事的胡安·包蒂斯塔·贝尔纳贝乌，其通信揭示了这种领事行动的范围与活力。

贝尔纳贝乌早期的报告，列举港内西班牙船只的进出，记录疫病暴发，并转述零星地方新闻。在任期最后五年，他的注意力几乎完全被私掠吸引——或按西班牙官员对美国海员劫掠的说法，是海盗行为。他向西班牙大使寄送详细信函，有时每日一封，不断催促拨款，以支付在私掠案件中代表西班牙政府的律师，并救济抵达巴尔的摩的西班牙海员；这些海员原在被捕船只上服役。他还极其详尽地描述自己资助的众多法律诉讼的进展，目的在于追回西班牙财产。

en: Bernabeu reserved special disdain for “the pirate Daniels.” He was incensed that Daniels returned with the
as a prize and was “strolling brazenly through the streets” while the lawyer hired to defend Spanish interests was struggling to get the vessel impounded and Daniels arrested for piracy.
Even after the marshal took charge of the

, Bernabeu was outraged that Daniels had been able to refit the ship and add to its armaments to make it ready to cruise again, and he fretted that lax port controls might allow Daniels to slip out of the harbor, as other privateers had done.

When Daniels was finally tried for piracy, in May 1819, Bernabeu met with lawyers to strategize about the case and attended all the sessions of the trial. Anticipating acquittal, he complained bitterly to the Spanish ambassador about the biased proceedings and predicted that Daniels would soon be “free and white as a dove” and the Spanish side thoroughly “mocked.”
After Daniels was acquitted and as the

suit proceeded on appeal, Bernabeu continued to track the captain’s activities, reporting in 1822 that Daniels had returned to Baltimore to recruit men for raiding in the Caribbean as an agent of Simón Bolívar.
zh: 贝尔纳贝乌尤其鄙视“海盗丹尼尔斯”。丹尼尔斯带着作为捕获物的
返港，竟“厚颜无耻地在街上闲逛”；与此同时，为维护西班牙利益而雇用的律师，却在艰难争取扣押船只，并以海盗罪逮捕丹尼尔斯。这令贝尔纳贝乌十分愤怒。
即使司法执行官已接管
，丹尼尔斯仍能修整该船、增添武装，准备再度巡航；贝尔纳贝乌对此怒不可遏，也担心松散的港口管制会让丹尼尔斯像其他私掠者一样，悄悄驶离港口。
1819年5月，丹尼尔斯终于因海盗罪受审时，贝尔纳贝乌与律师会面商讨策略，并出席每次庭审。他预料丹尼尔斯会被宣告无罪，便向西班牙大使激烈抱怨诉讼程序的偏颇，并预测丹尼尔斯很快就会“自由而洁白如鸽”，西班牙一方则会彻底遭到“嘲弄”。
丹尼尔斯获判无罪后，随着
诉讼进入上诉程序，贝尔纳贝乌继续追踪船长的活动，并于1822年报告说，丹尼尔斯已作为西蒙·玻利瓦尔的代理人返回巴尔的摩，为加勒比海劫掠招募人员。

en: Daniels’s exploits attracted so much attention partly because they involved the brazen capture of a Spanish warship. In other respects, his actions were unexceptional—as was Bernabeu’s response. At the same time he was tracking Daniels, Bernabeu was attending to dozens of other cases involving privateering voyages from Baltimore, many led by captains carrying commissions from polities in the Río de la Plata. In December 1819, Bernabeu reported that there were eight other ships in the harbor subject to ongoing litigation.
On a single day in that month, the district court heard matters involving four captures, including a motion about the
and one involving a ship captured by Joseph Almeida, a captain who had cruised with a commission from Artigas and was even more adept than Daniels at evading attempts to block his continued raiding.
zh: 丹尼尔斯的事迹如此引人注目，部分因为他公然捕获了一艘西班牙军舰。在其他方面，他的行动并无特殊之处，贝尔纳贝乌的回应亦然。追踪丹尼尔斯的同时，贝尔纳贝乌还在处理数十起涉及从巴尔的摩出发私掠航行的案件；许多船长持有拉普拉塔河地区政治体颁发的委任状。1819年12月，贝尔纳贝乌报告，港中另有八艘船卷入尚未了结的诉讼。
当月仅一天，地区法院就审理了涉及四宗捕获的事项，其中包括有关
的一项动议，以及涉及约瑟夫·阿尔梅达所捕获船只的事项。阿尔梅达曾持阿蒂加斯的委任状巡航，在躲避阻止其继续劫掠的措施方面，比丹尼尔斯还要老练。

en: Spanish demands to curb privateering and punish U.S. mariners as pirates formed the backdrop to negotiations over the Adams-Onís Treaty, even after negotiations were concluded in 1819. U.S. officials sometimes pushed disputes into the courts to lessen diplomatic tensions. When Luis de Onís, Spanish Minister in the United States, complained directly to Adams about Daniels’s arrival in Baltimore on a captured Spanish warship and demanded the ship’s return, Adams instructed him to have the Spanish consul file a libel for the return of the ship.
zh: 西班牙要求限制私掠、将美国海员作为海盗惩罚，构成《亚当斯—奥尼斯条约》谈判的背景；即使1819年谈判结束后，这一点仍然如此。美国官员有时把争端推入法院，以减轻外交紧张。西班牙驻美公使路易斯·德奥尼斯直接向亚当斯抱怨，丹尼尔斯驾驶一艘被捕西班牙军舰抵达巴尔的摩，并要求归还船只；亚当斯指示他，让西班牙领事提交海事诉状，请求返还该船。

en: British policy, meanwhile, was also developing in response to both geopolitics and specific disputes about privateering. In September 1821, a Spanish privateer had captured the

, a British brig carrying trade goods from Buenos Aires. The vessel was taken to Puerto Rico and condemned as good prize there. Initially, the British government assumed that the reason for the seizure was that the vessel had run a blockade, but it soon emerged that the prize had been condemned on the grounds that it was a foreign vessel trading in Spanish territory, an act prohibited under the Laws of the Indies. This logic confirmed merchants’ fears that the restoration of Fernando VII to the Spanish throne would bring a revival of Spanish power and the return of a closed imperial system. Profiting from a surge in exports, merchant houses were determined to maintain access to South American ports.

British officials threatened naval intervention to resolve tensions over the capture, and the Spanish government relented. Foreign Minister George Canning downplayed the tensions with Spain over the affair, describing the resolution as “a local remedy to a local grievance.”
zh: 与此同时，英国政策也在回应地缘政治与具体私掠纠纷的过程中发展。1821年9月，一艘西班牙私掠船捕获了

，这是一艘载着贸易货物、从布宜诺斯艾利斯出发的英国双桅横帆船。该船被送到波多黎各，并在那里被判为合法捕获物。起初，英国政府以为扣船的原因是它突破了封锁；但很快发现，法庭判其可被没收的理由，是它作为外国船在西班牙领土从事贸易，而《印度群岛法》禁止这一行为。这一逻辑证实了商人的忧虑：费尔南多七世重登西班牙王位，将带来西班牙权力的复兴，以及封闭帝国体系的回归。各商行正从出口激增中获利，决心维持进入南美洲港口的机会。
英国官员威胁以海军干预解决捕获引发的紧张，西班牙政府于是让步。外交大臣乔治·坎宁淡化了这件事引发的对西紧张关系，把解决方式描述为“对地方性不满的地方性补救”。

en: The

case strengthened the resolve of British officials to craft a policy of gradual recognition. The goal was to maintain Spain as an ally and to thread a course between mollifying Whig-supported commercial elites and placating counterrevolutionary powers.

The result was an ad hoc progression of steps toward partial recognition. Soon after news arrived in May 1822 of United States acts of recognition of Spanish states, the Board of Trade presented a bill, endorsed by the foreign secretary Lord Castlereagh, to admit vessels from new polities in South America to British ports. The Permanent Under-Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs, Joseph Planta, explained that the intent of the act was to “make as little fuss about it as we can” so as not to disturb relations with Spain.
In the summer of 1822, Castlereagh outlined steps to strengthening
recognition through the appointment of British consuls to Spanish America and the negotiation of commercial treaties.
zh: 案强化了英国官员制定渐进承认政策的决心。目标是维持西班牙作为盟友，同时在安抚辉格党支持的商业精英与安抚反革命强国之间寻找路线。
结果便是一系列迈向部分承认的权宜步骤。1822年5月，美国承认原西班牙辖下各国的消息传来后不久，贸易委员会便提出一项法案，获外交大臣卡斯尔雷勋爵支持，准许南美洲新政治体的船只进入英国港口。外交部常务次官约瑟夫·普兰塔解释，这项法令的意图是“尽可能少声张”，以免扰乱与西班牙的关系。
1822年夏，卡斯尔雷概述了通过任命驻西属美洲的英国领事，以及谈判商业条约，来强化
承认的步骤。

en: There were other signs, too, that the British government was prepared to quietly endorse a regional system of states. Castlereagh at one point proposed that European powers cultivate the formation of constitutional monarchies across South America. The proposal went nowhere: the French would not endorse it, Spanish officials would not brook independence in any form, and events in the Americas were in any case quickly outpacing such schemes. But Castlereagh’s dream of a continent of constitutional monarchies shows that even British officials attuned to counterrevolutionary pressures were anticipating the rise of a new Atlantic system. The question was not whether states would be established in South America but how quickly and in what form—and how they could be made to align with British interests.
zh: 还有其他迹象表明，英国政府准备低调支持一个区域国家体系。卡斯尔雷曾提出，欧洲列强应推动南美洲各地形成君主立宪制。这项提议没有结果：法国人不愿支持，西班牙官员不能容忍任何形式的独立，而且无论如何，美洲事态的发展已迅速超越这些方案。但卡斯尔雷关于一个由君主立宪国家组成的大陆的梦想，表明即使那些重视反革命压力的英国官员，也在预见一个新大西洋体系的兴起。问题不是南美洲会不会建立国家，而是建立得多快、采取何种形式，以及如何使这些国家与英国利益相协调。

en: Pressuring new states to contain privateering was part of this project of alignment. Much as Spanish diplomats were urging the United States government to ban privateering from U.S. ports, the British government sought to pressure South American officials to temper their sponsorship of privateering. Unlike Spanish diplomats in the United States, the British could not exercise influence through consuls, so their vehicle for delivering pressure on the new governments had to be the British Navy.

The Admiralty reported some success through naval channels. In Buenos Aires, the government moved to require privateers to register bonds of higher value before sailing, and the new Chilean government agreed to intervene to protect British vessels trading in Peruvian ports still under Spanish control. Yet the British government refrained from demanding more vigorous measures, instead opting for a system of limited intervention nestled within a formal policy of non-intervention.

To label as pirates all raiders licensed by the new governments would have called into question the status of the new entities as states, including their right to make war. That effect would have diminished the very claims of sovereignty that the British government was quietly seeking to reinforce.
